CSIA_CLAIM: Cross-sensor evidence can isolate sensor faults.
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: B04 Potter & Suman (parity space); B05 Chow & Willsky; B22 Dunia et al. (sensor validity index); B90/P23 automotive ESP sensor plausibility; B87 RAIM fault detection and exclusion
DOMAIN: aerospace redundancy management; FDI; process monitoring; automotive; GNSS integrity
WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: Parity-space and analytical-redundancy relations isolate a faulty sensor among redundant or physically related sensors. RAIM detects and excludes a faulty satellite measurement. ESP cross-checks yaw rate against a one-track vehicle model and wheel-speed kinematics in mass production.
WHAT_CSIA_DOES: v1 Dynamic Trust Graph: sensors as nodes, physical relations as edges, a Beta-recursion trust per node from residual consistency (csia/trust_engine). v2 SENSOR domain wraps it.
MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: None at the level of the idea. CSIA's trust recursion is one specific consistency-scoring scheme; B95 (2025) scores UAV sensor trust by consistency with kinematic models.
DIFFERENCE_SUBSTANTIVE_OR_TERMINOLOGICAL: TERMINOLOGICAL (Trust Coefficient ~ sensor validity index / reliability weight)
EVIDENCE_FOR_DIFFERENCE: No evidence of a difference that matters to the claim.
WHAT_WOULD_KILL_NOVELTY: Already killed by B04/B05/B22.
REQUIRED_FOLLOWUP: None for novelty. Cite B04, B05, B22 and B95 as antecedents of the trust graph.

CSIA_CLAIM: Cross-domain evidence can distinguish causes that local evidence cannot.
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: B58 Honeywell 777 central maintenance function (cascaded-fault screening across LRUs); B59/B60 VIPR / vehicle-level reasoning; B46/B47 Kobayashi & Simon (engine sensor vs component faults); P03 EPOS engine patent; B09 structural isolability
DOMAIN: avionics maintenance; IVHM; gas-turbine diagnostics; FDI theory
WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: Vehicle-level reasoners consolidate symptoms reported by many subsystems into one root cause, for example a power-bus failure that makes many LRUs appear failed. Engine diagnostics separate sensor faults from component and actuator faults using the engine's thermodynamic response. Structural analysis decides which faults are isolable given which signals.
WHAT_CSIA_DOES: v2 localization: domain plugins emit EvidenceRecords; a signature matrix of three-valued predicates eliminates hypotheses by domain; UNIQUE only for the last candidate standing and affirmatively confirmed.
MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: None in the core idea. CSIA's contribution, if any, lies in its verdict semantics (see C12, C13, C17), not in the claim that other domains add resolving power.
DIFFERENCE_SUBSTANTIVE_OR_TERMINOLOGICAL: TERMINOLOGICAL for the claim itself
EVIDENCE_FOR_DIFFERENCE: Repository evidence (engineering/v2/MATCHED_SCENARIOS.md) shows the claim holding in CSIA's own scenarios, which confirms an established principle rather than distinguishing it.
WHAT_WOULD_KILL_NOVELTY: Already killed by B58, B46 and P03.
REQUIRED_FOLLOWUP: Read B59 (VIPR final report) in full to compare output semantics, which the search summaries do not show.

CSIA_CLAIM: Vehicle dynamics can serve as an independent witness for actuator or telemetry faults.
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: B44 Maybeck MMAE on the VISTA F-16; B43 Zhang & Li IMM; P01 US 4,641,517; P03 EPOS; B92 Choi et al. control invariants; B93 SAVIOR; B48 Amoozgar et al. (quadrotor loss of effectiveness)
DOMAIN: flight control FDI; engine control; CPS security; multirotor FDI
WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: Banks of filters matched to sensor-failure and actuator-failure hypotheses discriminate the two from the vehicle's measured dynamic response. A 1987 patent decides whether a fault is in the sensors or the actuator by comparing against a model. Control-invariant and physical-invariant monitors detect falsified sensor data because the vehicle's dynamics do not follow. Quadrotor rotor loss of effectiveness is estimated from attitude dynamics.
WHAT_CSIA_DOES: DYN_T1_NOMINAL witness: mean body-rate deviation along the motor's thrust-loss axis in T1 (0-0.2 s after onset), thresholded, three-valued, and gated on the size of the local symptom.
MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: A deliberately scalar, per-motor, windowed witness fed into set elimination rather than a filter bank or a learned invariant. This is a design choice inside a known method.
DIFFERENCE_SUBSTANTIVE_OR_TERMINOLOGICAL: SUBSTANTIVE only as an engineering choice; TERMINOLOGICAL as an idea ('independent witness' ~ analytical redundancy relation / physical invariant)
EVIDENCE_FOR_DIFFERENCE: None beyond the design choice.
WHAT_WOULD_KILL_NOVELTY: Already killed by B44, P01, B92.
REQUIRED_FOLLOWUP: None for novelty.

CSIA_CLAIM: Controller compensation can itself be diagnostic evidence.
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: B55 ArduPilot thrust-loss and yaw-imbalance detection (motor output saturation); B99 closed-loop fault masking using controller-internal variables; B17 SDG diagnosis inside control loops; B21 Cristofaro & Johansen control allocation; P09 Amazon commanded vs measured RPM
DOMAIN: open-source autopilots; process control; control allocation; UAV patents
WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: A deployed open-source autopilot flags propulsion failure when a motor's commanded output saturates because the controller is compensating. Process-control FDD adds manipulated variables to the monitored set precisely because feedback masks faults in the outputs. SDG methods reason about steady-state propagation through control loops.
WHAT_CSIA_DOES: CTRL_T3_NOMINAL witness: kappa = allocator command on motor m / mean of the other motors; C_T3 = mean over 10-15 s minus pre-fault mean; under a compensated loss kappa -> 1/eta.
MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: A normalized, windowed, three-valued compensation witness that confirms or refutes a hypothesis inside set elimination, rather than a saturation alarm.
DIFFERENCE_SUBSTANTIVE_OR_TERMINOLOGICAL: SUBSTANTIVE as a formulation detail; TERMINOLOGICAL at the level of the claim
EVIDENCE_FOR_DIFFERENCE: B55 shows the concept fielded; the exact ratio statistic was not found, which is weak evidence of anything.
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH (the ArduPilot source was not read; process-control sources are snippet-level)
WHAT_WOULD_KILL_NOVELTY: Already substantially killed by B55 and B99.
REQUIRED_FOLLOWUP: Read ArduPilot AP_MotorsMatrix thrust-loss logic and PX4 failure detector source to state exactly how close the fielded logic is.

CSIA_CLAIM: Evidence usefulness changes over time during fault onset and compensation.
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: B37 Mosterman & Biswas, TRANSCEND; B38 Daigle et al. relative measurement orderings; B40 Meseguer, Puig & Escobet timed fault-signature matrices; B56 PX4 latching note
DOMAIN: qualitative/temporal model-based diagnosis; interval-observer FDI; autopilot practice
WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: TRANSCEND represents the predicted transient of each fault as a signature and monitors progressively until transient analysis is suspended in favour of steady-state analysis. Event-based diagnosis uses the temporal order in which measurements deviate. Timed signature matrices store occurrence order and occurrence time. PX4 latches motor failures because recovery removes the evidence.
WHAT_CSIA_DOES: Evidence regions T1 (0-0.2 s, dynamics) and T3 (10-15 s, compensation), fixed before data; outside its region a witness is NOT_APPLICABLE.
MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: None at the level of the claim.
DIFFERENCE_SUBSTANTIVE_OR_TERMINOLOGICAL: TERMINOLOGICAL
EVIDENCE_FOR_DIFFERENCE: None.
WHAT_WOULD_KILL_NOVELTY: Already killed by B37.
REQUIRED_FOLLOWUP: Read B37 and B38 in full; cite them as the direct antecedents.

CSIA_CLAIM: A diagnostic architecture should explicitly condition evidence on its temporal validity.
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: B37 TRANSCEND (transient vs steady-state analysis switch); B40 timed fault-signature matrices; B32 Brusoni et al. temporal model-based diagnosis; B67 R2U2 temporal-logic observers feeding diagnosis
DOMAIN: temporal MBD; FDI; runtime verification for health management
WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: Temporal MBD defines diagnosis over time-dependent behaviour and temporal constraints; TRANSCEND's signatures are valid for the transient and are replaced by steady-state reasoning; timed FSMs attach occurrence times to fault signals; R2U2 evaluates temporal properties before diagnostic reasoning.
WHAT_CSIA_DOES: Temporal validity as a per-evidence APPLICABILITY attribute: outside its window a witness is NOT_APPLICABLE and its predicate is None, never False; v2 elimination is unchanged.
MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: Representing temporal validity as an applicability value inside a three-valued consistency-based engine, so that out-of-window evidence can neither confirm nor refute. Whether this differs from mode- or context-dependent ARRs was not established.
DIFFERENCE_SUBSTANTIVE_OR_TERMINOLOGICAL: PARTLY SUBSTANTIVE (representation) / PARTLY TERMINOLOGICAL
EVIDENCE_FOR_DIFFERENCE: No searched source was seen to use exactly this representation, but search summaries do not show representations; weak evidence.
WHAT_WOULD_KILL_NOVELTY: A temporal/hybrid MBD paper that marks residuals as inapplicable outside mode- or time-windows (likely in the hybrid-diagnosis literature, B41/B42) would reduce this to KNOWN.
REQUIRED_FOLLOWUP: Read B41, B42 and Travé-Massuyès/Pulido work on mode-dependent ARRs and possible conflicts in hybrid systems.

CSIA_CLAIM: Structural hypothesis elimination can be combined with temporal evidence accumulation.
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: B37/B38/B39 TRANSCEND and QED with possible conflicts; B35 Lerner et al. hybrid DBN; B67/B68 R2U2; B69 Hipler, Leucker & Rodler (RV + MBD in LOLA); B42 HyDE
DOMAIN: temporal/hybrid MBD; Bayesian diagnosis; runtime verification
WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: Candidate sets are refined as fault signatures accumulate over time; DBNs track discrete fault variables jointly with continuous state; R2U2 combines temporal-logic observers with Bayesian-network diagnosis on UAS; a 2026 paper unifies runtime verification with model-based diagnosis in a stream language.
WHAT_CSIA_DOES: v2 localization is ATEMPORAL (docs/research/CROSS_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_SEED.md gap G1). XSYS-001 evaluates it at two fixed checkpoints (C1 = t0+0.2 s, C3 = t0+15 s) with windowed witnesses; no evidence accumulates across snapshots.
MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: CSIA implements LESS temporal accumulation than the prior art: two checkpoints rather than continuous refinement.
DIFFERENCE_SUBSTANTIVE_OR_TERMINOLOGICAL: NOT A DIFFERENCE IN CSIA'S FAVOUR
EVIDENCE_FOR_DIFFERENCE: Repository's own gap list G1-G3.
WHAT_WOULD_KILL_NOVELTY: Already killed by B37 and B67.
REQUIRED_FOLLOWUP: None for novelty; do not claim this.

CSIA_CLAIM: The system should preserve ambiguity when multiple causes remain consistent.
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: B28 Reiter (all minimal diagnoses); B29 de Kleer & Williams (GDE candidates); B62 TEAMS ambiguity groups; B64 MIL-STD-2165 isolation to N items; P06 RTX ambiguity resolution; B72 set-valued FDI; B96 Dempster-Shafer ignorance
DOMAIN: consistency-based diagnosis; testability; FDI; evidence theory; patents
WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: Consistency-based diagnosis returns every minimal diagnosis consistent with the observations without choosing among them; testability engineering specifies isolation to an ambiguity group; set-valued observers return every model not invalidated; DS theory keeps uncommitted mass.
WHAT_CSIA_DOES: AMBIGUOUS is a first-class verdict; a posterior leader without discriminating evidence is not reported as a cause ('A posterior is not confidence', docs/CSIA_MASTER_ARCHITECTURE.md section 3).
MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: Emphasis on NOT converting ambiguity into a unique claim through priors or ranking. VIPR and P06 rank ambiguity groups by belief; consistency-based diagnosis already refuses to.
DIFFERENCE_SUBSTANTIVE_OR_TERMINOLOGICAL: TERMINOLOGICAL relative to consistency-based diagnosis; SUBSTANTIVE only relative to probabilistic rankers
EVIDENCE_FOR_DIFFERENCE: B28/B29 already have the property.
WHAT_WOULD_KILL_NOVELTY: Already killed by B28.
REQUIRED_FOLLOWUP: None for novelty.

CSIA_CLAIM: The system should distinguish detection, isolation, certification and action authorization.
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: B07 Isermann & Ballé terminology (detection, isolation, identification); B87 RAIM (detection vs exclusion vs integrity availability vs alert-limit authorization); B66 Livingstone (mode identification vs reconfiguration); B81 ASTM F3269 (monitor vs recovery); B71 Bozzano et al. FDI requirements
DOMAIN: FDI terminology; GNSS integrity; autonomy; runtime assurance; formal FDI
WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: FDI terminology separates detection, isolation and identification; RAIM separates detecting a fault, excluding it, and whether integrity is sufficient for an operation (protection level vs alert limit); RTA separates monitoring from recovery; Livingstone separates diagnosis from reconfiguration.
WHAT_CSIA_DOES: Separate latencies for detection, isolation, certification (UNIQUE verdict) and action (not measurable, because CSIA issues no command); XSYS-001 reports them separately.
MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: 'Certification' as a named runtime stage with its own latency for root-cause attribution. RAIM's integrity-availability step is the analogue for navigation.
DIFFERENCE_SUBSTANTIVE_OR_TERMINOLOGICAL: MOSTLY TERMINOLOGICAL
EVIDENCE_FOR_DIFFERENCE: RAIM already has the separation for position; no source was found that names a certification stage for cross-domain root-cause attribution, which is weak evidence.
WHAT_WOULD_KILL_NOVELTY: Any IVHM or RTA paper that distinguishes 'fault isolated' from 'isolation certified for use by the controller' kills it.
REQUIRED_FOLLOWUP: Search SAE ARP6803 / AIR6900 / JA6268 (IVHM standards) and HUMS credit guidance (FAA AC 29-2C MG-15).

CSIA_CLAIM: Runtime adaptation should be constrained by the strongest conclusion actually justified by the available evidence.
CLOSEST_PRIOR_ART: B87 RAIM/ARAIM (operation permitted only if protection level < alert limit); B84 ConSerts; B85 dynamic safety cases; B77 Paoli & Lafortune safe diagnosability; B09 passive FTC fallback when the fault is not isolated; spacecraft safe-mode practice; B66 Livingstone; B80/B81 RTA
DOMAIN: navigation integrity; safety assurance; DES supervision; FTC; autonomy
WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: Navigation operations are authorized only when integrity evidence bounds the error below an alert limit. Conditional safety certificates grant guarantees only when runtime evidence meets demands. Safe diagnosability requires detection before a forbidden behaviour so that reconfiguration can be forced. FTC textbooks fall back to passive/robust control when isolation fails. Spacecraft enter safe mode when a fault cannot be isolated.
WHAT_CSIA_DOES: A design commitment ('the layer issues no command'); function eligibility states which functions remain justified and which domain limits them. No authorization mechanism is implemented in CSIA and none is tested by XSYS-001.
MATERIAL_DIFFERENCE: A verdict-typed authorization (actions keyed to UNIQUE / AMBIGUOUS / UNSUPPORTED across heterogeneous domains) is proposed, not built.
DIFFERENCE_SUBSTANTIVE_OR_TERMINOLOGICAL: SUBSTANTIVE IF BUILT; currently a proposal
EVIDENCE_FOR_DIFFERENCE: No implementation; no evaluation.
WHAT_WOULD_KILL_NOVELTY: RAIM already embodies the principle for one domain; a paper binding root-cause verdicts to permitted actions would kill the rest.
REQUIRED_FOLLOWUP: If pursued: formalize verdict-to-authorization rules and compare against RAIM, ConSerts and safe diagnosability.

CSIA_CLAIM: A 'nominal response' witness may refute a hypothesis only if the local symptom predicts a response a genuine fault would make detectable (gated negative evidence).

WHAT_PRIOR_ART_ALREADY_DOES: Fault models allow a component to be exonerated when its faulty behaviour would have produced a different observation; the 'no exoneration' default exists because absence of a symptom is not evidence of health unless the fault would have shown.
